chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: All people are free, except for the one who confesses upon himself with slavery, and he is an adult from a slave or a slave girl; and the one against whom is testified with slavery, whether he was young or old.'

key_terms.أَحْرَارٌ: Free (plural of حُرّ), indicating the default state of liberty
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the default legal status of humans in Shia jurisprudence according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) attributes this principle to Imam Ali (AS), highlighting the Prophetic tradition that liberty is the innate default state of humanity, with slavery being a specific legal exception rather than a natural condition. This narration underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that emancipation is the norm, reinforcing the social justice ethos of the Ahl al-Bayt by limiting the scope of bondage to those with proven lineage or explicit acknowledgment.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying that the people, all of them are free, except for the one who confesses upon himself with the slavery, and he was an adult from a slave, or a slave girl; and the one against who is testified with the slavery, whether he was young or old’.
